children: Kodiak AI is piloting autonomous trucking deliveries with long-haul freight company DTL Transport in California.

The pilot comes after Kodiak received a heavy-duty autonomous vehicle testing permit from the California Department of Motor Vehicles in August, the company said Thursday. The DMV approved new regulations earlier this year that allow for heavy-duty autonomous trucks to operate on the state's public roads.

Through the partnership with DTL Transport, Kodiak's autonomous trucks are hauling perishable goods between Fresno, Calif. and a distribution center in Los Angeles. The route spans about 225 miles, mostly on California State Route 99 and Interstate 5, the company said.
A human safety driver will remain behind the wheel during the companies' initial work together, they said.
The companies said the results from the pilot will allow them to consider further opportunities in California and beyond.

DTL Transport, which specializes in hauling produce for several large grocers, said it is exploring ways that autonomous technology could allow it to grow capacity when its existing fleet can't keep up with demand.
